stemMd: Why would using only the shortest observed distance be misleading?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Walking times never depend on route conditions.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Residents had deliberately invented the shortcut.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The informal path was always faster for every traveller.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It would overlook differences in accessibility and weather conditions.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The formal map was perfect in every respect.

explanationMd: A shortcut’s physical length does not capture whether it is usable by a particular person or after rain. Recording both routes and their conditions avoids treating one observed experience as universal.

distractorRationale.c: Wheelchair access and mud make that universal claim unsupported.
